reason: The weighty bills form one restrictive entry and residence policy: tighter enforcement against illegal stay (1, 9), Basic Laws on immigration and status (2, 6, 40), the Citizenship and Entry temporary order that bars family unification with spouses from the Palestinian territories, plus bills to repeal it (3, 5, 8, 11, 12, 25, 27, 30, 34, 35, 37), Entry into Israel amendments (4, 13, 19, 21, 28), deportation of infiltrators (14, 15), and narrowing Law of Return rights for family members (7, 10). All labels point the same way as the statement: agreeing means more restriction. The statement's general wording covers them. It names the largest specific block (Palestinian spouses) and its cost (separated families). Law of Return family members (about 7% of the weight) and caregiver visa bills are minor, and they still fit the general 'entry and residence of foreigners' framing. No change needed.
